Activation Phase: In a player's Activation Phase they Activate each of their models one at a time, in any order. An Activation runs: start of Activation, start of Move, Move, end of Move, end of Activation, with special rules resolving at each step. A model must finish its Activation before another begins. Every model must be Activated if able, but a model may do nothing; models that cannot be Activated (for example because they are Engaged in Combat) skip the steps.
Broken Army: The Break Point is half the models in the starting Army and never changes (50 models: 25; 13 models: 6.5). If at the start of a turn the casualties are greater than the Break Point, the Army is Broken from then on: each time a model Activates it must first take a Courage Test, passing means it stays and fights, failing means it flees and is removed as a casualty. Models that cannot Activate (Engaged in Combat, or held by a special rule or Magical Power) do not test.
Moving Models: A model Moves up to its Move Value in inches, always measured from the same point on the base, in any direction and not necessarily in a straight line. Models cannot Move through other models and need room for their base to fit through gaps, though players may agree that a model obviously fits. Facing does not matter (except for War Beasts and Chariots); do not rotate a model to gain an advantage.
Charging: To fight an enemy a model must Charge it, and needs Line of Sight to it at the start of its Move. Move into base contact with the target within the Move Value: both models are then Engaged in Combat and the Charging model's Activation ends. Models Engaged in Combat cannot be Activated in the Move Phase, unless they stop being Engaged before their turn to Activate. The order in which models are Activated matters, as models can block or free each other.
Charges and Control Zones: Four rules: (1) a model that enters an enemy Control Zone must Charge that model if able (it may keep moving around within the zone to reach another part of the base, and chooses between zones it enters at once); (2) a model Engaged in Combat has no Control Zone; (3) once a Charging model has entered a Control Zone it ignores other models' Control Zones to Charge its original target; (4) a model Charging an enemy that has lost its Control Zone may ignore the Control Zones of enemies it would be impossible to Charge.
Engaged in Combat: A model that has Charged into base contact with an enemy is Engaged in Combat with it. Engaged models cannot be Activated in the Move Phase (unless they stop being Engaged before their turn to Activate), lose their Control Zone while in Combat, and must fight in the Fight Phase.
Obstacles: Obstacles are linear objects (walls, hedges, barricades, fallen trunks). A model crosses an Obstacle equal to or less than half its height automatically; a taller one needs a Jump Test (Obstacle up to its own height) or a Climb Test. Use the model's true height, from head to feet including the base, ignoring unusual poses.
Jumping: A model may Jump an Obstacle up to its own height (taller needs a Climb Test): Move into base contact and roll a D6. 1: stumbles and fails, stays put and its Activation ends. 2-5: success, placed on the other side; if now in an enemy Control Zone it must Move the minimum distance to Charge that model (if it has Move Value), otherwise its Move ends. 6: bounds across and continues its Activation. Horizontal distance counts towards the Move, vertical does not.
Leaping: A model may Leap a gap no wider than twice its height (or a river), if it has the Move Value to reach the other side: Move to the edge and roll a D6. 1: falls to the bottom of the gap, suffers Falling Damage, becomes Prone and its Activation ends. 2-5: success, placed on the other side of the gap; if in an enemy Control Zone it must Move the minimum distance to Charge that model, otherwise its Move ends. 6: effortlessly bounds across and continues its Activation.
Prone Models: A Knocked-to-the-Ground model becomes Prone (mark it with a Prone marker). It has no Control Zone and counts as half height for Line of Sight. It can only Crawl 1" (no Jump, Leap or Climb Tests) or Stand Up at the cost of half its Move Value (then Move or Charge as normal); a standing model can Lie Down for the same cost. It cannot Charge but can be Charged; if it wins the Duel Roll it makes no Strikes and may Stand Up instead, and if it loses it Backs Away and is always considered Trapped. Models can Jump over Prone models as an Obstacle (a roll of 1 means they must Charge it).
Reinforcements: Reinforcements enter during their player's Activation Phase of the Move Phase, after every model on the board has Activated: choose a point on the specified board edge and Move on from it. They cannot Charge that turn. In Matched Play a whole Warband enters together, Captain first, Followers within 3" of that point; if there is no room for all of them they enter next turn with a +1 bonus to the roll for the entry point.
Water Features: Water features are discussed before play as Shallow Water or Deep Water, and a model cannot Lie Down in them. Shallow Water counts as Difficult Terrain (Open Ground for Cavalry, Monster and War Beast models); a Prone model that starts its Activation in it must take a Swim Test first. Entering or starting an Activation in Deep Water also needs a Swim Test (D6: 1 sinks and drowns, 2-5 Move up to half the remaining Move Value, 6 Swim Strongly for all of it). Modifiers: Cavalry +1; heavy armour or heavy Dwarf armour -1; shield (not light shield) -1; banner -1. Models in Deep Water cannot Shoot.
Line of Sight: Check from the model's head (model's-eye view, or a 1mm line with a tape measure); a model has a 360 degree view. A model has Line of Sight only if it can see part of the target's head, body, arms or legs; banners, weapons, wings and tails do not count, and terrain modelled onto a base never blocks it. A model always has Line of Sight to itself. Use the model's true height, ignoring tall bases or low conversions.
Keywords: Each profile has Race keywords (Man, Elf, Orc), Faction keywords (Gondor, Rohan, Mordor; a model may have several) and Unit Type keywords (Infantry, Cavalry, Monster, Hero...). Rules in bold name the keywords of the models they affect, and a model needs all the keywords listed. A model made of several parts (rider and Mount) has separate keywords for each part, so a rule for Man models affects the rider but not the Mount.
Shooting Phase: In a player's Shooting Phase they Shoot with each of their models in any order. A model's Shoot runs: start of Shoot, make a single Shooting Attack with one Missile Weapon, end of Shoot. A Shooting Attack: check Line of Sight, roll To Hit, make any In The Way Tests, roll To Wound, remove casualties. Shooting up or down from an elevated position: measure from the Shooting model's base to the closest part of the target when shooting down; base to base when shooting up.
Moving and Shooting: A model that Moved more than half its Move Value in the preceding Move Phase cannot Shoot, nor can one that attempted a Jump, Leap, Climb or Swim Test, nor Prone models. A model that Moved up to half its Move Value worsens its Shoot Value by 1 for that attack (4+ becomes 5+); a natural 6 always hits. Difficult Terrain counts: a model there can Move only a quarter of its Move Value and still Shoot.
Taking Shots Together: Several models Shooting at the same target can take their shots together: roll one dice per shooter, work out the hits, then roll To Wound. Use different coloured dice for shooters with different Shoot Values, obstructions or To Wound rolls, and make your intent clear to the opponent.
Pairing Off Combats: At the start of the Fight Phase every model Engaged in Combat is Paired Off into a Combat, so that no Combat has multiple models from both sides. Models are Paired Off only with a model they are in base contact with, none may be Paired Off in a way that stops them being Engaged, and where a model could be Paired Off in several ways the player with Priority decides.
Duel Roll: To decide a Combat each side rolls a D6 (a number of D6 equal to its Attacks, using the highest) and the highest roll wins. Order: gather dice (a different colour for each model with modifiers or Might Points), declare weapon abilities such as a two-handed weapon, roll, apply modifiers, use re-rolls (banners, special rules), use Might Points, determine the winner.
Loser Backs Away: The loser Backs Away 1" in a straight line in a direction its controller chooses, through enemy Control Zones but not into base contact. It is not a Move, so it is not slowed by Difficult Terrain and can be done by models that cannot Move; it cannot cross Obstacles or take Jump, Climb or Leap Tests. A loser at the edge of a drop with nowhere else to go goes over the edge (Strikes first, then Falling Damage). A model that cannot Back Away is Trapped.
Trapped: A model that cannot Back Away after losing a Duel Roll is Trapped (usually against terrain or other models): it stays in place while the enemy Strikes, then the enemies are separated slightly. A rule that asks whether a model is Trapped checks it when the rule applies: it is Trapped if it would be unable to Back Away should it lose the Duel Roll, not counting a Back Away that a friend's Make Way would allow.
Make Way: A friendly model may Make Way, a Move of up to 1" (not slowed by Difficult Terrain, possible while Prone), so that an ally can Back Away the full 1". It cannot be done by a model Engaged in Combat or unable to Move, over an Obstacle, with Jump, Climb or Leap Tests, or over a cliff edge. Only one model can Make Way for an ally; if that is not enough the ally is Trapped. It is optional.
Multiple Attacks: A model with multiple Attacks that wins the Duel Roll makes that many Strikes. Against several enemies it may resolve them one at a time (each fully, including Might and special rules, before the next) or all at once (declare each Strike's target first, then roll all together). Be clear with your opponent about how the Strikes are used.
Barriers: A Barrier (wall, hedge, barricade) is defendable if at least half the attacker's height and the defender can see over it. A defender in base contact with it has a Control Zone that extends over the Barrier, and enemies cannot cross it there; they must Charge, placing the attacker in base contact with the Barrier opposite the defender (still counting as Engaged and in base contact). Only one model may Charge a defender over a Barrier. Strikes are made before Backing Away; if the attacker wins it must pass an In The Way Test for each Strike. A defender who loses and survives does not Back Away (the attacker does); a slain defender lets the attacker cross. If the defender is also Charged from its own side the Barrier gives no protection. A Barrier offers no protection against an attacker more than twice its size; Prone models cannot defend one.
Cavalry: A Cavalry model is a rider and its Mount. A separated rider swaps the Cavalry keyword for Infantry; an Infantry model that buys a Mount becomes Cavalry (only one Mount each). Only models that start with the Cavalry keyword or buy a Mount can ride. Line of Sight is checked from the rider. In Combat the model fights as one, using the highest Fight Value, Attacks and Strength of rider and Mount (even mixing them), but it is the rider fighting, so the rider's special rules and modifiers (such as a two-handed weapon) apply.
Separated Mounts: When a Mount loses its rider (slain, knocked off or dismounted) it immediately takes a Courage Test with its own Courage: if passed it stays (replace the model with an unridden Mount), if failed it flees. A Mount with Attacks 0 (a horse) automatically fails. A Cavalry model knocked Prone makes the rider suffer Knocked Flying on the Thrown Rider Table; if there is no room, rider and Mount share the space and enemies may Strike either. A separated rider cannot remount during the game.
Barge: A Monster that wins may Barge instead of Striking: all enemies in the Combat (including Supporting models) Back Away 3" (and Make Way 3") in the order and direction the Monster's controller chooses, going the full 3" where possible, otherwise as far as possible and then knocked Prone. The Combat then ends; the Monster Moves D3+3" and may Charge again (fighting again that phase). A Monster cannot Barge in a turn in which it takes part in a Heroic Combat.
Hurl: A Monster that wins may Hurl one enemy in the Combat with lower Strength (the others Back Away as normal). Roll D3 and add the Strength difference: the Hurl Distance. The Monster takes an Intelligence Test (a Monster that is a Mount may use its rider's, if better): passed, it picks an enemy in Line of Sight within the Hurl Distance as target; failed, the opponent chooses. The Hurled model suffers two Strength 6 hits (and Knocked Flying if Cavalry); if it survives it is placed next to the target and knocked Prone. The target is knocked Prone if Strength 5 or less and suffers a Strength 6 hit. With no target, the Monster picks a point instead. The Combat then ends, and a Monster cannot Hurl in a turn in which it takes part in a Heroic Combat.
Trample: A War Beast Moves by Trampling and must Move if able: pivot on its centre to face any direction, then Move its full Move Value in a straight line, ignoring Control Zones. Models it touches take the Impact Hits on its profile (both parts of Cavalry); a slain model lets the Trample continue, otherwise the War Beast stops, Charging and Engaged. It crosses Obstacles of 2" or less and Difficult Terrain or water, but cannot enter woodland, Jump, Climb, Leap, Lie Down or defend a Barrier. Hitting uncrossable terrain or the board edge stops it; hitting another War Beast means three Strength 8 hits each way. If Charged by a combined Strength higher than its own it cannot Trample. It cannot Trample the turn it arrives by Reinforcements.
Stampede: Each time a War Beast suffers a Wound it takes a Courage Test with its Commander's Courage (the Commander may use Might and Will); if failed it Stampedes at the start of its next Activation, and must be Activated first. A War Beast with no riders at the start of its Activation tests with its own Courage. In a Stampede the opposing player pivots it and Tramples it its full Move Value; hitting uncrossable terrain or another War Beast means three Strength 8 hits each way, leaving the board removes it and its riders, and its riders cannot Shoot that turn. It then reverts to its controller.
Chariot Charge: A Chariot Moves by a Chariot Charge and must Move if able: pivot up to 45 degrees with the Chariot Pivot Template, then Move up to its Move Value in a straight line, pivoting again after each full 4". It ignores Control Zones; models it touches take the Impact Hits on its profile, a slain model lets it continue, otherwise it stops, Charging and Engaged. It halves Move in Difficult Terrain and rolls a D6 per Charge there (a 1 is a Wound); it cannot Jump, Climb, Leap, Swim, Lie Down or defend a Barrier. Hitting an Obstacle means three Strength 6 hits each way. It can forego the Charge to pivot instead, and cannot Chariot Charge the turn it arrives by Reinforcements.
Chariots and Heroes: A Hero upgraded to ride a Chariot is still a single model with the Hero's Fight Value, Strength, Courage and Intelligence used if better, plus their Attacks added to the Chariot's. Might can influence the Chariot's rolls (not Impact Hits), Will can Resist Magical Powers and affect Courage Tests, and Fate can prevent Wounds on the Chariot. The Hero is wounded separately but cannot be targeted separately; if the Chariot is slain the Hero is dismounted as if Knocked Flying. Kills made by the Chariot are the Hero's. The Hero cannot declare a Heroic Combat on the Chariot unless stated, and may Dismount like a Cavalry model.
Might, Will and Fate: A Hero has Might, Will and Fate characteristics: finite stores of points that are reduced when spent. A rule that regains a point cannot take a Hero above its starting number unless it says so, and a rule that allows something free of cost works even at 0.
Modify Dice Rolls: A Hero spends one Might Point to raise one dice of a roll made on its behalf by 1 (never above 6, never to lower). Might is decided after all dice, re-rolls and modifiers, so it is always the last thing to affect a roll. Opposing Heroes in a Duel Roll bid back and forth, starting with the side currently losing. A Hero can only alter its own rolls, so roll each Hero's dice separately or in a different colour.
Can I Use Might?: Might can improve a Hero's own: Jump, Climb, Leap, Swim, Thrown Rider and In The Way Tests; Duel Rolls (after modifiers and re-rolls); To Hit Rolls; To Wound Rolls it causes directly (Strikes, Shooting Attacks, Magical Power hits; a second value such as 6+/4+ carries over), but not indirect ones such as Falling Damage or a Thrown Rider Test of a foe; Courage and Intelligence Tests; Casting and Resist Tests; and Fate Rolls. It cannot alter other rolls, such as the roll-off for a tied Duel Roll, unless a special rule says 'Might can be used to alter this roll'.
Will: A Hero spends Will Points to pass a Courage Test (+1 per point, can be mixed with Might), to Cast a Magical Power (one extra D6 per point on the Casting Test) and to Resist a Magical Power (one extra D6 per point on the Resist Test).
Fate: Whenever a Hero suffers a Wound it may spend a Fate Point and roll a D6: on a 4+ the Wound is prevented. If it fails the Hero may spend another, one at a time, each fully resolved first; Might can raise a Fate Roll but must be decided before the next Fate Point. A single successful Fate Roll prevents all the damage of a multi-Wound or instant-kill Strike. Fate cannot save a Hero that flees the board after a failed Courage Test.
Heroic Actions: A Hero spends a Might Point to declare a Heroic Action in the Declare Heroic Actions step of the Move, Shoot or Fight Phase (its phase is in brackets after its name): one per phase per Hero, none at 0 Might unless a rule makes it free, and none if off the board. The player without Priority declares first, then players alternate declaring or passing until both pass in succession; a declaration cannot be changed or taken back. Heroic Move and Heroic Combat change the order of the phase: if both sides use them the player with Priority rolls a D6 (1-3 Evil first, 4+ Good first) and they alternate. A model benefits from only one Heroic Action of each type per turn, except a successful Heroic Combat followed by a second Heroic Combat (which it fights but cannot Move in again).
With Me: A Hero making a Heroic Move may shout With Me as soon as it is Activated: friendly models within 6" of its starting position are affected and, after the Hero finishes its Activation, each either Activates (ending within 6" of the Hero, otherwise stopping where it is) or forgoes its Activation, and cannot Activate again that Move Phase. The Hero shouts it even if it cannot Move. If the Hero is removed as a casualty, the Heroic Move and With Me are cancelled. A second Hero within 6" that also declared a Heroic Move loses it. Affected models may leave the board only if the Hero does.
Heroic Combat: The Hero's Combat is resolved first. If it wins and all enemies in it are removed as casualties, the Hero and friendly models that were in the Combat (not War Beasts or Chariots) may immediately Move or Charge (and fight again in the order the player with Priority chooses); Combats are then Paired Off again. A model benefits from one Heroic Combat per turn. If opposing Heroes both declare one in a Combat, whichever side clears the Combat counts as successful.
At the Double: A Hero making a Heroic March may shout At the Double as soon as it is Activated: friendly models within 6" of its starting position add 3" to their Move Value (Infantry, Chariot, War Beast) or 5" (Cavalry or Fly), but cannot Charge, and must finish their Activation within 6" of the Hero (otherwise they stop, or forgo their Activation if they cannot). Affected models may choose not to Activate, forgoing it. If the Hero is removed as a casualty the Heroic March is cancelled. A model can be affected by only one At the Double per turn.
Heroic Accuracy: The Hero gains the Sharpshooter special rule until the End Phase and may re-roll failed In The Way Tests when Shooting (including the test for which part of a Cavalry model is hit). It cannot be declared if Engaged in Combat or unable to Activate. The Hero may shout Take Aim, extending the re-roll to friendly models within 6", which need not target the same enemy.
Heroic Challenge: The Hero names an enemy Hero within 6" of the same Heroic Tier or higher. While Engaged with it, the challenger gains +1 Attack (Duel Roll and Strikes) and +1 To Wound against it, and gains 1 Might Point if it slays it (not above its starting level). The target may accept (gaining the same benefits; both must Charge each other when Activated if possible; no other Hero can challenge either; they cannot challenge anyone else until one is slain) or decline (no benefits, and it cannot challenge the challenger back). A Hero can have only one unresolved challenge at a time.
Using Magical Powers: A model with Magical Powers and Will Points can Cast one (and only one) per Activation, at any point after start-of-Activation abilities: before, during or after its Move, in the turn it Charges, even if it does not Move. A Prone model or one that cannot Activate cannot Cast, and a Flying model must land. A power targets a specific model, all models within a range, or no model; an Engaged model can be targeted. A Cavalry model is targeted as a whole unless the power says the caster must choose rider or Mount (before the Casting Roll). Good models cannot Cast if they risk wounding a friend. Line of Sight and range are needed to target an enemy.
Making a Casting Roll: To Cast, state the power and target and spend Will Points, rolling a D6 per point (all declared beforehand); if any dice equals or beats the power's Casting Value, it is Cast. A Hero may spend Might to improve the result, but before the target tries to Resist.
Resisting a Magical Power: After the Casting Roll, before applying the effects, a targeted model may spend Will Points to make a Resist Test, a D6 per point (chosen beforehand): if any equals or beats the highest Casting score, the power is resisted. Might may improve it. A natural 6 on a paid Will Point regains that point (not for free Will such as Heroic Resolve or Resistant to Magic). If a power targets a part of a Cavalry model, either part may Resist. A model only indirectly affected cannot Resist.
Spear: An Infantry model armed with a spear can Support a friendly model in a Combat (see Supporting), and can use the spear as a hand weapon when Engaged in Combat.
Throwing Weapons: A throwing weapon can make a Shooting Attack in the Shoot Phase even after a full Move. Alternatively, once per turn, it can be thrown during the Move Phase as the model Charges: stop 1" away, Shoot (without the Moving and Shooting penalty), then if the target is not slain Charge it, or if it is slain Move on as normal (even Charging another target). A model that starts in the target's Control Zone need not Move first. Throwing weapons do not count towards the Bow Limit, but only one third of an Army's models may have them unless stated. Throwing spears follow the same rules with a different profile.
Banner: A banner has a 3" area of effect. A Combat is affected if a friendly Engaged or Supporting model is within range of a friendly banner and has Line of Sight to it: one friendly model in that Combat may re-roll a single dice in the Duel Roll (one re-roll per side however many banners; not on a dice it is winning with). The bearer must be standing (a Prone bearer gives no benefit) and suffers -1 to Duel Rolls. A banner limited to keywords works only for those models. A Warrior bearer removed as a casualty may pass the banner to a friendly Warrior in base contact (not Prone or Engaged) that could carry one, dropping the wargear it cannot also have.
The One Ring: A Ringbearer can put the Ring on at any point in its Activation (not if unable to Activate) and becomes Invisible; a mounted model's Mount bolts and the model takes a Thrown Rider Test. At the start of each Activation wearing it, roll a D6 (Might can help): on a 1-2 the opponent Moves the Ringbearer (may Charge it, passing Terror tests) but cannot make it take the Ring off, pick up or put down items, harm itself or leave the board; all other actions stay under its controller. Taking the Ring off needs a Courage Test (retry next turn). In Matched Play, if it is the last model on its side and wearing the Ring, it is removed as a casualty. With several Ringbearers the highest of Sauron, Isildur, Bilbo, Frodo, Bilbo (Ageing Hobbit), Gollum carries it.
Active and Passive Special Rules: Every special rule is Active or Passive. An Active rule needs the user to act or think (Mighty Blow, Expert Shot, Woodland Creature, Shielding, war horns) and cannot be used by a model that cannot Activate (unless it was merely Charged) or that cannot use Active rules, such as under Transfix. A Passive rule always applies, even if the model cannot Activate (Terror, Horse Lord, Resistant to Magic).
Timing of Special Rules: When several rules trigger at the same step: the same player chooses the order; if both players have some, the player with Priority uses one or passes, then the other, alternating until both pass in succession (a rule that must be used cannot be passed). If both have rules that come into play before Priority is decided, the player who had Priority last turn goes first.
Light Objects: Light Objects (keys, rings, draughts, weapons) are shown by a 25mm marker. A model picks one up by Moving into base contact, and can keep Moving; Cavalry must Dismount to do so. During the Move Phase it can be passed to a friendly model in base contact, but it is Moved once and passed once per turn. A model Engaged in Combat cannot pass or drop it; a dropped one is placed in base contact (not overlapping another base). The killer of a carrier slain by a model in base contact takes it, otherwise it stays where the carrier was.
Heavy Objects: Heavy Objects (demolition charges and similar) are carried by Moving into base contact. A carrier's Move Value is halved and it puts the Object down in base contact when done Moving. Two friendly models in base contact before either Activates can Move together without halving (the Object ends in contact with both) but cannot Charge. A Heavy Object cannot be Moved twice in a Move Phase or overlap bases. Cavalry cannot carry one; Monsters keep their full Move Value.
Passengers: A Passenger rides a Cavalry model without being its rider (mostly Narrative Play, or Matched Play only if a profile says so). It is a separate model for counting purposes, cannot Activate, Shoot or contribute to a Combat while mounted, and is affected by rules that affect rider and Mount. It can Dismount at any point in the Cavalry model's Move (and does so if the rider Dismounts). A Shooting Attack that would hit the rider rolls a further D6: 1-3 hits the Passenger. Strikes can be made against it like the rider, and it takes a Thrown Rider Test when the Mount or rider is slain. Mounting (Narrative only): Move into contact and roll a D6: 1 fails, 2-5 succeeds but neither Moves further, 6 succeeds and the Cavalry model can still Activate.
Sentries: In some Narrative Scenarios Sentries Activate first in their Move Phase, after rolling a D6 on the Sentry Chart: 1 it cannot Move; 2-3 the opponent Moves it up to half its Move Value; 4-5 its controller Moves it up to half; 6 its controller Moves it normally. Until the alarm is raised they cannot Shoot or use powers and rules that target enemies. The alarm is raised in the End Phase if a Sentry is within 3" of an enemy it has Line of Sight to, or was hit by a Shooting Attack and not slain; Sentries then act normally.
Fighting at Night: In night Scenarios models see only 12 inches: they cannot target enemies beyond that with Shooting Attacks, Magical Powers or abilities, and Shooting Attacks at models in the dark gain +1 To Wound. Siege Engines may still fire further but only hit on a 6 (their Area Effect gets no +1). Models illuminated by a rule or power (such as Blinding Light) can be targeted at any range, without the +1; models with Cave Dweller see normally and do not give the +1.
Moving a Siege Engine: A Siege Engine has no Activation and cannot Move by itself; friendly models Move it: three models for a Large Siege Engine, two for a Small one (a Monster counts as three). They must all be in base contact at the start of the Move Phase and Activate together, Moving it up to the Move Value of the slowest of them, and it may be rotated about its centre as part of the Move (or rotated without Moving). It cannot Move through Difficult Terrain, cross Barriers or take Jump, Climb, Leap or Swim Tests, nor be Moved while an enemy is in base contact with it. A Siege Engine with the Static special rule cannot be Moved or rotated.
Firing a Siege Engine: A Siege Engine Shoots if it was not Moved in the preceding Move Phase and enough unengaged crew are in base contact (two for a Large one, one for a Small one), and no enemy is in base contact with it. It needs the target in range (many have a minimum and a maximum range), in Line of Sight and in its 45 degree Arc of Sight. Roll To Hit with the highest Shoot Value among the firing crew, with -1 if the Engine was rotated in the Move Phase. A miss does nothing. Against a Siege Target a hit is a hit; against a Battlefield Target a hit rolls on the Scatter Table to find the actual target, which may be out of range or out of the Arc.
Attacking a Siege Engine: A Siege Engine can be shot at like other models and can be targeted by Magical Powers and special rules, but ignores every effect except damage. If at the End Phase an enemy model is in base contact with it, has done nothing that turn except Move (no Shooting Attack, Magical Power or Combat) and was not affected by a Magical Power, it can disable the Engine, reducing its Wounds to 0 and removing it. A Siege Engine never counts as a model for the Army's model count or Break Point, has no Control Zone, cannot be Engaged in Combat or knocked Prone, and counts as Strength 6 for rules that refer to Strength.
Castles and Fortresses: A fortification is its walls and its gates and doors. Walls taller than a model cannot be Climbed (Swift Movement models may, if they reach the top), so attackers need a Siege Ladder or Siege Tower; the rules do not allow smashing down walls. Gates and doors can be destroyed or Moved through during play.
Attacking Gates and Doors: Gates and doors can be shot at (Strength 5 or more may damage them, Strength 4 or less cannot) or attacked in the Fight Phase by a model in base contact at the end of the phase that has not been Engaged in another Combat (Supporting models likewise). No Duel Roll is made: the attacker wins, Strikes against it as if it were Trapped, and a gate at 0 Wounds is destroyed, so either side can pass. Monsters cannot use Brutal Power Attacks on them. Characteristics (Defence/Wounds): Fortress/Castle Gate 10/3; Dwarven Door 9/3; Heavy Armoured Door 9/2; Armoured Door 8/2; Heavy Door 7/2; External Domestic Door 6/2; Internal Domestic Door 5/1.
Fighting Up Ladders: A model may Charge up a Siege Ladder against a defender on the walls and is Engaged in Combat with it, remaining at the top of the ladder if the defender is in base contact with the battlements there (it may Charge only one enemy while on the ladder; nobody can Support a model on a ladder, though defenders may Support their ally). If it wins, the opponent Backs Away and a slain defender lets it Move onto the walls at the ladder's position. If it loses, after Strikes it rolls a D6 instead of Backing Away, and on a 1-3 falls and suffers Falling Damage; every other model climbing that ladder rolls too.
Siege Tower: A Siege Tower is tall enough for its ramp to reach the battlements, at most 4" wide across the ramp. Infantry (not Monsters) can be deployed in or on it. Friendly models push it 6": six Infantry (a Monster counts as six) plus one more per model in or on it, pushing from the rear or side. It lowers its ramp when it Moves into base contact with the fortress in the Move Phase. It has Defence 10 and 4 Wounds, is a Battlefield Target and, if destroyed, everything in or on it suffers Falling Damage.
Supporting: A model (an Infantry model with a spear or pike) that is not Engaged and in base contact with a friendly model of the same base size or smaller can Support it, adding a single dice to its Duel Roll using the Supporter's own Fight Value and, if it wins, a single Strike using its own Strength (against a different target in a Multiple Combat if wanted). Supporting models are not part of the Combat: they cannot be Struck, knocked Prone by a Cavalry Charge or benefit from a Heroic Combat, and do not count for numbers. A model supports one Combat per Fight Phase, only if not already Engaged (except after moving in a successful Heroic Combat), and not if Prone, unable to Activate, or having made a Shooting Attack that turn. A Hero Supporting may use Might, but cannot Support if it declared a Heroic Action.
Strike: A Strike is a To Wound Roll made by the winner of a Duel Roll: its Strength against the target's Defence on the To Wound Chart. A successful roll takes 1 Wound off the target (0 Wounds: slain and removed as a casualty); a failed roll does nothing. A model makes a number of Strikes equal to its Attacks.
Impact Hits: Hits suffered by every model that a Trampling War Beast or a Charging Chariot comes into base contact with. The number and Strength of the hits are on its profile; a Cavalry model takes them on both rider and Mount.
Turn Sequence: Each turn is played as five phases in this order: Priority Phase (roll for Priority), Move Phase, Shoot Phase, Fight Phase and End Phase (resolve lingering effects and clear tokens and dice). In the Move and Shoot Phases the player with Priority Activates all their models first, then the other player.
Scatter: When a Siege Engine's To Hit Roll fails the shot misses. Against a Siege Target a hit simply hits; against a Battlefield Target a hit rolls on the Scatter Table to find the model actually hit. A shot can scatter onto a model beyond the Engine's maximum range or outside its Arc of Sight.
Knocked Flying: Result 1 on the Thrown Rider Table: the rider suffers one Strength 3 hit and, if it survives, is placed Prone. It cannot Activate, Move, Shoot, make Strikes or Cast Magical Powers for the rest of the turn. If the Mount survived the rider is placed in base contact with it; if the rider is Engaged in Combat it fights as a Prone model.
